# Regional flooding after overnight storms

Federal investigators said the storm caused widespread flooding across several counties. Residents described overnight evacuations as water rose along the river. Local officials opened shelters and asked drivers to avoid submerged roads. Meteorologists warned that additional rain could extend the emergency into the weekend. Hospitals reported minor injuries and no confirmed fatalities as of late afternoon. Utility crews restored power to thousands of homes after trees fell on distribution lines. The governor requested federal disaster assistance and praised first responders. Community groups collected food, water, and clothing for displaced families. Transportation agencies posted detours around washed-out bridges. Schools closed Friday so buildings could be inspected for water damage. Insurance companies set up claims centers near the hardest-hit neighborhoods. Environmental scientists sampled runoff for contaminants from industrial sites. Farmers said fields remain too wet for harvest equipment. The National Weather Service kept a flood watch in effect through Sunday night. Neighbors organized boat rescues for people stranded on upper floors. City engineers inspected levees and pumping stations after the peak crest passed.
